title: Introduce residency-negotiator middleware, KMS jurisdiction gateway, and RBAC attenuation
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Add residency-negotiator middleware to enable per-request region negotiation, introduce a KMS jurisdiction gateway for tenant-key routing and consent logic, and add RBAC attenuation layer for operator-limited delegation. Backwards-compatible rollout behind feature flag.
body:
Summary: This PR adds three coordinated components: (1) residency-negotiator middleware that centralizes per-request residency negotiation and provides a pluggable policy hook for routing, (2) kms-jurisdiction-gateway — a service adapter that proxies KMS calls and enforces jurisdiction + consent checks and transparent audit stamping, and (3) rbac-attenuator — a lightweight in-process filter that reduces operator-level privileges based on route/residency context.

Motivation: Customers running in regulated regions require finer-grained controls for KMS usage and operator delegation. Existing region-pin knobs were scattered; this unifies negotiation and introduces guardrails so operator tokens cannot be used to escalate cross-jurisdiction access.

Design highlights: residency-negotiator is a request-scoped middleware that emits a structured ResidencyDecision (region, fallback policy, required-consent), persisted to request context and outgoing audit headers. kms-jurisdiction-gateway implements a safe proxy pattern: it validates the decision, consults the KMS routing table, and either issues a direct KMS call or delegates to fallback keys. rbac-attenuator applies attribute-based attenuation: if an operator token contains an operator role, attenuation reduces allowed actions (no key unwrap, no cross-region wrapping) and annotates decisions in audit.

Feature flagging: gated behind experimental.feature.residency_negotiator (default off) for gradual canary.

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-582) - [x] unit tests for negotiation logic - [x] integration test with kms-jurisdiction-gateway in docker-compose - [x] e2e scenario that simulates tenant with region=eu and operator in us - [x] feature flag added and documented in config schema

Commits (high level): 1) add residency-negotiator middleware, context structs and tests (3 commits) 2) implement kms-jurisdiction-gateway adapter and routing table + mocks 3) add rbac-attenuator plugin and integrate with authn pipeline 4) tests: add integration and e2e harness updates 5) docs: operational runbook and config examples

Changed files (overview): - pkg/middleware/residency/negotiator.go (+tests) - pkg/middleware/residency/policy.go - services/kms/gateway/adapter.go (+routing table, tests) - services/kms/gateway/consent_cache.go - auth/attenuators/rbac_attenuator.go (+unit tests) - internal/config/feature_flags.go - docs/runbooks/residency-negotiator.md - docs/config/residency-example.yaml - ci/integration/docker-compose.residency.yml - go.mod / go.sum

Notes on implementation: - Residency decisions are purely advisory for hosted mode; in Dedicated/Private we call into the installed kms-gateway hook which can be configured to enforce. - Consent is a first-class bit in the decision (consent_required: boolean) and is stamped into X-Redwood-Res-Decision header for downstream audit processors. - The KMS gateway supports plugin adapters for cloud KMS providers (AWS/Azure/GCP) and sane defaults for multi-provider fallback. - RBAC attenuation uses existing policy matcher to compute an allowed-action set then intersects it with attenuation rules; this keeps authorization deterministic and explainable.

Review conversation (summary): - Ethan Zhao (reviewer): "Can we ensure the KMS gateway never performs key unwrap when the ResidencyDecision.region != key.region? Also add metrics for consent failures." Author reply (Priya): "Added server-side check to refuse unwrap for cross-region keys and incremented kms_gateway.consent_failures counter. Unit+integration tests added." - Maya Alvarez: "Concern about feature flag scope in Dedicated installs — we should provide an operator-config switch rather than runtime flag in config service." Author: "Updated config schema with operator_config.residency_negotiator.enabled and added a validation hook during installer runs. Documented in installer notes." - Samir Rao: "Make attenuation tolerant of stale operator claims; add a short TTL cache for claim signatures." Author: "Added claim-signature cache in auth/attenuator to reduce validation latency and fallbacks on cache-miss; tests added."

CI and checks: - unit: pass - integration (docker-compose.residency): pass after 2 reruns (flaky DB migration race fixed) - lint: pass (golangci fixes applied) - e2e: pass (added a focused scenario) - security-scan (dependency-scan): initially flagged an out-of-date aws-sdk indirect dep; bumped and re-run -> pass

Observability and metrics added: - residency.negotiation.latency (histogram) - residency.decision.count (labels: outcome, region) - kms_gateway.consent_failures (counter) - rbac.attenuation.applied (counter)

Rollout plan: - Canary: enable feature in internal infra region for 5% of traffic for 48h via feature flag. - Monitor: increased alerting on residency.decision.failure rate and kms_gateway.consent_failures; no SLA impact expected. - Migrate: after 2 stable weeks and signoff from security, flip default.

Backwards compatibility and migration notes: - Default behavior unchanged when feature flag is off. - Existing tenants without residency metadata will fall back to legacy routing. - Installer notes: Private/Dedicated customers should opt into the gateway plugin and supply jurisdiction routing table; docs added at docs/runbooks/residency-negotiator.md

Testing notes: - Added targeted unit tests for edge cases: unknown-region, consent-absent, operator-token-attenuated. - Integration tests cover multi-provider fallback and consent caching.

Security review: - SEC-210 performed threat modeling for cross-region unwrap and operator escalation; recommendations implemented (strict unwrap checks and audit stamping).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged by Maya Alvarez.

Follow-ups (linear tickets): - ENG-613: Integrate KMS gateway metrics with Console dashboards - ENG-647: Expand adapter plugin tests to include HSM-backed key flows - SEC-221: Hardening audit envelope to include residency decision HMAC

Example config snippet (docs/config/residency-example.yaml): feature_flags:
  experimental:
    residency_negotiator: true operator_config:
  residency_negotiator:
    enabled: true    kms_gateway:
      routing_table: /etc/redwood/kms-routing.yaml      consent_cache_ttl: 30s

If you want to run locally: see docs/runbooks/residency-negotiator.md for docker-compose and test harness instructions. If this change needs to be reverted quickly: feature toggle is available and rollback documented in the runbook.
